paper_metadata.title: Revealing the mechanical behavior of Ti48-xZrxHf26Nb26 high-entropy alloy through zirconium content variations

evidence.quote: Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) composed of Ti, Zr, Hf, and Nb have emerged as promising materials for high-temperature aerospace applications

The exploration into the mechanical behavior of the Ti48-xZrxHf26Nb26 ( x = 14, 18, 22, 26, 30, 34) RHEAs has yielded crucial insights into its structural and compositional impact on mechanical properties.

process_steps.input_state: raw materials Ti, Zr, Hf, Nb

evidence.quote: The Ti48-xZrxHf26Nb26 alloys (x = 14, 18, 22, 26, 30, 34) were prepared in an arc melting furnace (WK-II, Opto-electronics Co., China) under an Ar atmosphere using a non-reactive tungsten electrode.
The as-cast alloys were then suction-cast in vacuum into dimensions of 10 × 10 × 50 mm3, and sealed in quartz tubes under vacuum.
The as-cast alloys were then suction-cast in vacuum into dimensions of 10 × 10 × 50 mm3, and sealed in quartz tubes under vacuum.
Subsequently, the sealed alloys were homogenized at 1200°C for 24 h in the annealing furnace (TF1, Carbolite, Germany) to reach an equilibrium state before quenched in ice water.
After post-annealing, these alloys manifest an equiaxed grain structure with significantly coarse grains, averaging 600–700 μm.
Evidently, these alloys exhibit a predominant singular body-centered cubic (BCC) phase within the detectable limits of XRD resolution.
The alloys consistently exhibit a singular body-centered cubic (BCC) phase across compositions.
The TiZrHfNb alloys manifesting as an equiaxed grain structure with notably coarse grains by post-extended annealing. The measured average grain size, spanning from 600 μm to 700 μm
Notably, the alloys of 14Zr and 34Zr exhibit deeper dimples. However, the 14Zr alloy showcases smaller dimple sizes yet demonstrates greater elongation at fracture
The lattice distortion within this phase underscores its influence on the mechanical behavior.

Conversely, alloys with higher Zr content display increased tensile strength but reduced toughness, evidenced by an elongation of 16.05 % for 34Zr alloy.
Alloys rich in Ti exhibit superior toughness, exemplified by an elongation of 17.83 % for 34 at% Ti (i.e. 14Zr alloy)
Alloys with higher Ti content demonstrate superior toughness, exemplified by an elongation of 17.83 % for 34 at% Ti (14Zr alloy).
Additionally, the 26Zr alloy emerges with the peak tensile strength at 695.25 MPa
Chemical short-range orderings (CSROs) and solid-solution strengthening significantly contribute to tensile strength, with the peak reaching 695.25 MPa for the 26Zr alloy.

The dominance of CSROs and solid-solution strengthening mechanisms emerges as the primary contributors to the determined tensile strength characteristics in the TiZrHfNb RHEAs.
The strengthening mechanism attributed to chemical short-range orderings (CSROs) primarily arises from the interactions between Ti-Zr and Hf-Nb pairs within the Ti48-xZrxHf26Nb26 RHEAs [11,12].
The primary strength of TiZrHfNb RHEAs stems from SROs and lattice distortions, with less contribution from atomic bonding.
